request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Hospital Course:
The patient, a 35-year-old Japanese woman, presented to our facility in gestational week 29 with low back pain, weakness of her lower extremities, and impaired liver function with low platelet count. An epidural hematoma was detected in her thoracic spinal canal, which was confirmed by MRI findings, resulting in emergency decompression. The patient was diagnosed with HELLP syndrome and underwent an emergency Cesarean section to end the pregnancy. Post-operatively, the patient experienced bilateral lower limb paralysis and complete urinary retention, leading to diagnosis of grade B injury according to the ASIA/ISCoS classification. A surgical intervention was performed successfully, and the patient’s condition improved gradually.
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course and Procedures:
The patient underwent an emergency Cesarean section to terminate the pregnancy due to HELLP syndrome, which resulted in bilateral lower limb paralysis and complete urinary retention. The MRI detected an epidural hematoma in the thoracic spinal canal which was removed by neurosurgical decompression. The patient's condition improved gradually after the surgery.

Condition at Discharge:
The patient's lower limb sensation improved to a score of 8 out of 10, and muscular strength limited to a slight improvement. The patient was classified as ASIA/ISCoS grade C.

Follow-up Plans:
The patient was discharged and scheduled for follow-up visits with the neurosurgical and obstetric departments to monitor her progress.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
CODE: O14

The principal diagnosis is HELLP syndrome, which the team treated by emergency Cesarean section. ICD-10-AM classifies HELLP syndrome under O14 (pregnancy-induced hypertension with oedema or proteinuria, including HELLP), in the pregnancy and childbirth chapter. The spinal epidural haematoma and the paralysis were complications, not the chief reason for the episode.
